title: Cosine similarity was quietly sabotaging our incident search.
body:
Cosine similarity was quietly sabotaging our incident search.

Every incident in the store looked alike to the embedder — same product vocabulary, same log-line cadence — so "nearest" meant "vaguely on-topic," not "actually similar." Similar-incident recall sat around 30%.

Two changes fixed it. I masked the identifiers that were dominating the vectors — region, timestamp, host — so the model stopped keying on boilerplate. Then I put hybrid retrieval in front: BM25 for the exact tokens, vectors for the semantics, fused.

Recall went from ~30% to 80%+ on similar-incident lookup.

The lesson I keep relearning: when your data is homogeneous, pure vector search can't discriminate. You have to strip what's shared before you can find what's actually alike.
